newsitem.title: GERMANY: Most German publishers unharmed by new media - poll.
newsitem.headline: Most German publishers unharmed by new media - poll.

text.p: Most German publishers do not believe the boom in electronic media has harmed their traditional business, according to an industry opinion poll released on Tuesday.

However 20 percent of newspaper and magazine publishers and 10 percent of scientific and trade journal publishers say some of their business has been siphoned off by the increasingly competitive electronic publishing market.

The poll was conducted by the Fraunhofer institute for labour market and organisation (IAO), in which 500 German publishers were asked to give their views on trends in the industry in light of the rise of news media in publishing.

The IAO said publishers could make their online services profitable by introducing advertising, retail sales of information or online distribution to their Internet business, but it warned that many users are put off by online ads.
The biggest hurdles before a worldwide information community lie in a lack of security, which poses a need for international treaties and contracts, said the IAO.

Success in the future will be determined by publishers' ability to serve as "information brokers", filtering data and presenting it in an attractive way. Smaller publishers will be reliant on cooperation with more established firms.
The IAO added that a study on behalf of the European Commission said the market share of electronic media in the publishing business would grow to between 5 and 15 percent by the year 2005.
The use of online services in private households should also grow explosively in the next five to 10 years, according to the EU study.

Management consulting firm Diebold said that publishers and media companies posted 200 million marks ($117 million) in Internet sales in 1996, and it predicted that turnover should reach two billion marks next year, the IAO said.
